SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p224/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p224/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p224/r1.claim: The denunciation after the death scene reports conditions of the afterlife, linking these verses to the opening oath by Resurrection.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p224/r1.anchor: 1- أن هذه الآيات وقعت بعد قوله: {والتفت الساق بالساق * إلى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ المساق} وهذا النفي والإخبار فيها، إنما هو في الآخرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p224/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p224/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p224/r2.claim: The wrongdoer both commits denial and turns away, then leaves faith and prayer undone; the two kinds of failure provoke reproach for wrongful action and neglected good.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p224/r2.anchor: والنفس هنا قدّمت التكذيب والتولّي: {ولاكن كَذَّبَ وتولى} وأخَّرت التصديقَ والصلاة {فَلاَ صَدَّقَ وَلاَ صلى}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r1.claim: Not believing in the Resurrection explains the person's failure to believe and pray; this links the conduct to his earlier question about when the Hour will come.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r1.anchor: فهو مستبعد له مكذب به فهو لم يصدق ولم يصل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r2.claim: The deeds reported as sent ahead and left behind are disbelief and turning away on one side, and delayed faith and prayer on the other.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r2.anchor: فإنه قدم التكذيب والتولي وأخر التصديق والصلاة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r3.claim: Faith is inward assent, while belief and denial are matters of the heart, speech, and limbs: he lacked inward belief, openly denied, and turned away from action, so he lacked faith's reality.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r3.anchor: فهو لم يصدّق بالجنان {فَلاَ صَدَّقَ} وكذّب باللسان، كما قال تعالى: {ولاكن كَذَّبَ}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r4.claim: Failure to pray and turning away connect with the later attempt to offer excuses when questioned about those deeds.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r4.anchor: وارتبط عدم الصلاة والتولي بإلقاء المعاذير

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r5.claim: His denial also links to the question about gathering bones, since belief in the Last Day is a central article of faith.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r5.anchor: والإيمان باليوم الآخر من أهم أركان الإيمان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r6.claim: The person loves the immediate life and leaves the afterlife, which accounts for his denial and turning away.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r7.claim: Had he believed and prayed, he would have joined the radiant faces; because he denied and turned away, he belongs with the grim-faced people.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p225/r7.anchor: لو صدق وصلى لكان من أصحاب الوجوه الناضرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r1.claim: The agent of neither believed nor prayed is omitted as another mark of the surah's haste.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r1.anchor: 6- عدم ذكر فاعل {فَلاَ صَدَّقَ وَلاَ صلى}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r3.claim: It negates two acts of obedience: belief and prayer.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r3.anchor: ونفت اثنتين من الطاعات في قوله: {فَلاَ صَدَّقَ وَلاَ صلى}

AKHFASH:v2p558/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p558/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p558/r1.claim: فلا صدق ولا صلى means he did not believe and did not pray, as in ذهب فلا جاءني ولا جاءك.
AKHFASH:v2p558/r1.anchor: وقال {فلا صدق ولا صلى} أي: فلم يصدق ولم يصل. كما تقول "ذهب فلا جاءني ولا جاءك".

NAHHAS:v5p92/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p92/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p92/r9.claim: Here lā is negative, not conjunctive; grammarians reject “I struck Zayd, not I struck Amr” because the second clause resembles a supplication.
NAHHAS:v5p92/r9.anchor: لا ههنا نفي وليست بعاطفة ولا يجوز عند النحويين ضربت زيدا لا ضربت عمرا والعلة في ذلك

NAHHAS:v5p92/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p92/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p92/r10.claim: The verse means that he neither believed nor prayed.
NAHHAS:v5p92/r10.anchor: وفي الآية المعنى لم يصدق ولم يصل

RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r1.claim: The passage describes denial of the fundamentals of faith, abandonment of prayer, and a swaggering return to family; the unbeliever merits blame and punishment for leaving prayer as for unbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r1.anchor: أنه تعالى شرح كيفية عمله فيما يتعلق بأصول الدين وبفروعه ، وفيما يتعلق بدنياه

RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r2.claim: One view takes the subject as generic humanity, linked to the sura’s earlier references to the human being and the question of the Resurrection’s time.
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r2.anchor: أنه كناية عن الإنسان في قوله : { أيحسب الإنسان ألن نجمع عظامه }

RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r3.claim: A second view says the passage was revealed concerning Abū Jahl.
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r3.anchor: أن الآية نزلت في أبي جهل

RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r6.speaker: أهل العربية
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r6.claim: Arabic grammarians say lā here functions as lam: the verse means he did not believe and did not pray.
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r6.anchor: قال أهل العربية : { لا } ههنا في موضع لم فقوله : { فلا صدق ولا صلى } أي لم يصدق ولم يصل

RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r7.speaker: الكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r7.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says Arabs do not use this lā construction alone; it is followed by another negative either stated or understood.
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r7.anchor: قال الكسائي : لم أر العرب قالت في مثل هذا كلمة وحدها حتى تتبعها بأخرى

RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r8.claim: The precedent in al-Balad reads lā iqtahama as “he did not scale”; after an interruption, the freeing of a slave and feeding a poor person complete the implied coordinated negation.
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r8.anchor: فلا اقتحم العقبة } ( البلد : 11 ) أي لم يقتحم

RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r9.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r9.claim: Others analyze lā iqtahama as an interrogative exhortation: “Would he not have scaled it?” or “Why did he not scale it?”
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r9.anchor: ومنهم من قال التقدير في قوله : { فلا اقتحم } أي أفلا اقتحم ، وهلا اقتحم

STUDYQURAN:75:31/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:31/r1.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:75:31/r1.claim: The person who neither confirmed nor prayed may be Abū Jahl.
STUDYQURAN:75:31/r1.anchor: He refers to Abū Jahl or ʿAdī ibn Rabīʿah

STUDYQURAN:75:31/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:31/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:75:31/r2.claim: Alternatively, the person may be ʿAdī ibn Rabīʿah.
STUDYQURAN:75:31/r2.anchor: He refers to Abū Jahl or ʿAdī ibn Rabīʿah

STUDYQURAN:75:31/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:31/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:75:31/r3.claim: The person did not affirm the Quran’s revelation or Muhammad’s prophethood.
STUDYQURAN:75:31/r3.anchor: He did not confirm the revelation and the prophethood of Muhammad

STUDYQURAN:75:31/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:31/r4.speaker: Q, Z
STUDYQURAN:75:31/r4.claim: Ṣaddaqa can instead mean that he did not give charity, ṣaddaqa mālahu.
STUDYQURAN:75:31/r4.anchor: can be understood to mean that he did not give charity

TAB-FULL:v23p522/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p522/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p522/r1.claim: The person neither believed in God’s Book nor performed prayer for God.
TAB-FULL:v23p522/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {فلا صدق ولا صلى} [القيامة: 31] لا صدق بكتاب الله، ولا صلى لله

TAB-FULL:v23p522/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p522/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p522/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses the first phrase as not believing in God’s Book or praying to God, and the next as denying the Book and turning from obedience.
TAB-FULL:v23p522/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {فلا صدق ولا صلى} [القيامة: 31] لا صدق بكتاب الله

TABATABAI:75:31-36/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r1.claim: The pronouns refer to the human mentioned earlier; denied belief means affirming the Qur’an’s true call, and denied prayer is worship through salat, religion’s central pillar.
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r1.anchor: الضمائر راجعة إلى الإنسان المذكور في قوله { أيحسب الإنسان } الخ

TABATABAI:75:31-36/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r2.claim: The man rejects the Qur’an’s beliefs and does not pray; instead he denies the call and turns away.
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r2.anchor: فلم يصدق هذا الانسان الدعوة فيما فيها من الاعتقاد ولم يصل لربه أي لم يتبعها فيما فيها من الفروع وركنها الصلاة

TABRISI:75:29-36/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:29-36/r10.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:75:29-36/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan says he gave no charity and did not pray to God.
TABRISI:75:29-36/r10.anchor: لم يصل لله { ولكن كذب } بالله { وتولى } عن طاعته عن الحسن

TABRISI:75:29-36/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:29-36/r11.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:75:29-36/r11.claim: Qatāda says he did not affirm God's Book or pray to God; instead he rejected the Book and Messenger and turned away from faith.
TABRISI:75:29-36/r11.anchor: لم يصدق بكتاب الله ولا صلى لله ولكن كذب بالكتاب والرسول وأعرض عن الإيمان عن قتادة

BURSEVI:v10p197/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p197/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p197/r10.claim: The person did not affirm what must be believed about the Messenger and the Qurʾān revealed to him.
BURSEVI:v10p197/r10.anchor: الإنسان ما يجب تصديقه من الرسول والقرآن الذي نزل عليه

BURSEVI:v10p197/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p197/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p197/r11.claim: Here لا has the force of لم with a past verb; Arabic commonly repeats لا in paired negation, while using it alone is rare.
BURSEVI:v10p197/r11.anchor: فلا ههنا بمعنى لم وإنما دخلت على الماضي لقوة التكرار

BURSEVI:v10p197/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p197/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p197/r12.claim: An alternative reading is that he did not give the alms due on his wealth, with فلا صدق ماله understood as withholding zakāt.
BURSEVI:v10p197/r12.anchor: أو فلا صدق ماله بمعنى لا زكاة

BURSEVI:v10p197/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p197/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p197/r13.claim: If صدق means zakāt, its mention before prayer suits Meccans’ withholding from the needy and failure to urge feeding during acute need; prayer comes later to preserve the verse endings.
BURSEVI:v10p197/r13.anchor: ولعل وجهه ما كان كفار مكة عليه من منع المساكين وعدم الحض على طعامهم

BURSEVI:v10p197/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p197/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p197/r14.claim: He did not perform the prayer made obligatory for him.
BURSEVI:v10p197/r14.anchor: ما فرض عليه وفيه دلالة على أن الكفار مخاطبون بالفروع

BURSEVI:v10p197/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p197/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p197/r15.claim: The verse shows that unbelievers are accountable for subsidiary religious duties in punishment: a disbeliever merits blame and punishment for abandoning prayer as for abandoning faith, though worldly performance is not required of him.
BURSEVI:v10p197/r15.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أن الكفار مخاطبون بالفروع في حق المؤاخذة

THALABI:v10p90/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p90/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p90/r6.claim: The person who neither believed nor prayed is Abu Jahl.
THALABI:v10p90/r6.anchor: فلا صدق يعني أبا جهل ولا صلى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p523#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p523#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p523#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and the exegetes identify the person as Abu Jahl.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p523#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬2) والمفسرون (¬3): يعني: أبو جهل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p523#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p523#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p523#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says Abu Jahl did not believe in the Messenger’s mission and did not submit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p523#2/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: يقول: لم [يصدق] (¬4) أبو جهل بالرسالة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p523#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p523#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p523#2/r3.claim: Muqatil says Abu Jahl did not believe in the Qur’an and did not pray to God.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p523#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p523#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة، المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p523#2/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Mubarrad read the phrase as not believing or praying; lā can negate the past as well as the future, as in 90:11, a hadith, and Tarafa’s line.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p523#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة (¬8)، والمبرد (¬9): أي لم يصدق، ولم يصل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r2.claim: The person who neither affirmed nor prayed is Abū Jahl.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r2.anchor: { فلا صدق ولا صلى } يعني: أبا جهل لعنه الله.

ELMALILI:75:31-35/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r1.speaker: ekser müfessirîn
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r1.claim: Most exegetes take ṣaddaqa as affirmation of faith, which Elmalılı says is also its apparent sense.
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r1.anchor: Bunu ekser müfessirîn iman mânasına “tasdîk”ten olmak üzere tefsir etmişlerdir ki zâhiri de budur.

ELMALILI:75:31-35/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r2.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r2.claim: Some interpreters, as reported by Abu Hayyan, understand ṣaddaqa as giving alms: he gave no charity.
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r2.anchor: Ebû Hayyân’ın dediği gibi bazıları da “sadaka”dan olarak, “sadaka vermedi” diye tefsir etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:75:31-35/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r3.claim: Elmalılı favors the almsgiving sense because otherwise v32 merely reinforces the denial; ṣaddaqa can mean almsgiving, matching al-Muddaththir 74:43–44.
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r3.anchor: Evvelkinde وَلَٰكِن كَذَّبَ mücerred tekid gibi kalmış olacağından bu mâna daha faydalıdır.

ELMALILI:75:31-35/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r4.claim: The fā links these clauses to the preceding account of the sinner absorbed in worldly pleasure, who asks when the Resurrection will come, and frames his eventual return to God.
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r4.anchor: İkisinde de bunun “fâ” ile yukarıya rabtı şu mazmûnu ifade eyler

ELMALILI:75:31-35/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r5.claim: The sinner neither affirmed the hereafter nor did work for God, gave no alms or prayer, denied God, the Messenger, Qur’an, and afterlife, and turned away from truth and obedience.
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r5.anchor: Çünkü o dünyada ilerisini ne tasdik etti, ne Allah için bir amel işledi, ne sadaka verdi, ne namaz kıldı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:31/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:31/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:31/r1.claim: The passage criticizes disbelievers who still refuse the truth, Qur’an, and Prophet and avoid worship despite extensive proofs of God’s unity, resurrection, and the punishment awaiting deniers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:31/r1.anchor: hâlâ gerçeği kabul etmemekte, Kur’an’ı ve peygamberi tasdik etmemekte direnen, Allah’a kulluğunu arzetmekten kaçınan inkârcı tutum

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:31/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:31/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:31/r2.claim: The unbeliever refuses revelation and worship and deliberately lies about the truth and its messenger.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:31/r2.anchor: O inkârcı tip, vahyi onaylamaya, Allah’a kulluk etmeye yanaşmaz; hakkı, hak davetçisini inatla yalanlamaya kalkışır

BURHAN:v4p355/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p355/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p355/r1.claim: Here لا means لم and therefore enters only on a past verb: he neither believed nor prayed.
BURHAN:v4p355/r1.anchor: الرابعة إن تكون بمعنى لم ولذلك اختصت بالدخول على الماضي

BURHAN:v4p353/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p353/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p353/r2.claim: La is usually repeated in a coordinated negative, but may appear once, as in the statement that he neither believed nor prayed.
BURHAN:v4p353/r2.anchor: والأكثر تكرارها وقد جاءت غير مكررة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فلا اقتحم العقبة ﴾

BURHAN:v3p458/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p458/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p458/r1.claim: Muqābala pairs something with a counterpart that shares some qualities and differs in others; unlike ṭibāq, it often extends beyond opposites and can include non-opposites. Ibn al-Athir treats ṭibāq as one kind of muqābala.
BURHAN:v3p458/r1.anchor: وهي قريبة من الطباق والفرق بينهما من وجهين

BURHAN:v3p458/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p458/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p458/r2.claim: The three types are analogical, contradictory, and divergent; divergent pairing is strongest in ambiguity and interpretive force, contradictory is next, and analogical is third.
BURHAN:v3p458/r2.anchor: وهي ثلاثة نظيري ونقيضي وخلافي والخلافي أتمها في التشكيك وألزمها بالتأويل

BURHAN:v3p458/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p458/r3.speaker: أبو الفضل يوسف بن محمد النحوي القلعي
BURHAN:v3p458/r3.claim: Al-Qal'i claims the whole Qur'an displays muqābala, showing wise relations among created, temporal, spiritual, and divine realities in varied patterns.
BURHAN:v3p458/r3.anchor: وذكر الشيخ أبو الفضل يوسف بن محمد النحوي القلعي أن القرآن كله وارد عليها

BURHAN:v3p458/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p458/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p458/r6.claim: The verse pairs صدق with كذب and صلى, meaning approached, with تولى.
BURHAN:v3p458/r6.anchor: وصلى الذي هو أقبل ب تولى

ITQAN:v2p500/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p500/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p500/r5.claim: When lā precedes an ungoverned nominal clause or a past verb, it must be repeated; the two lā particles in 75:31 illustrate the past-verb case.
ITQAN:v2p500/r5.anchor: أو فعلا ماضيا لفظا أو تقديرا وجب تكرارها

ITQAN:v4p394/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p394/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p394/r3.claim: The verses “he neither believed nor prayed” were revealed concerning Abu Jahl.
ITQAN:v4p394/r3.anchor: 5759 ﴿ فلا صدق ولا صلى ﴾ الآيات نزلت في أبي جهل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p631#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p631#2/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p631#2/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba interprets لا here as لم: the person neither believed nor prayed.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p631#2/r4.anchor: أي : لم يصدق ولم يصل ، قاله ابن قتيبة .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#2/r1.claim: He paraphrases the verse as saying that the man did not believe and did not pray.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#2/r1.anchor: {فلا صدق ولا صلى} أي لم يصدق ولم يصل (2) .

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292/r1.claim: Lā can function with the sense of lam; here the man neither believed nor prayed.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292/r1.anchor: لا: تكون بمعنى لم، قال الله تعالى: فلا صدق ولا صلى (31) [القيامة: 31] ، أي لم يصدق ولم يصل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292/r2.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292/r2.claim: In the anonymous war poem, lā afaʾnā means lam nafiʾ, 'we did not turn away from our plunder.'
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292/r2.anchor: قال الشاعر : وأي خميس لا أفأنا نهابه ... وأسيافنا يقطرن من كبشه دما؟! أي لم نفىء نهابه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292/r3.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292/r3.claim: In the second anonymous poem, lā alamma means lam yulim, 'he has not committed sins.'
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292/r3.anchor: وقال آخر : إن تغفر اللهم تغفر جما ... وأي عبد لك لا ألما أي لم يلم بالذنوب

SAMIN-DURR:75:31/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:31/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:31/r1.claim: لا before a past verb is common Arabic negation with the force of لم; cited poems demonstrate the usage, and the first two suffice as evidence.
SAMIN-DURR:75:31/r1.anchor: " لا " هنا دخلت على الماضي، وهو مستفيض في كلامهم بمعنى: لم يصدق ولم يصل

SAMIN-DURR:75:31/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:31/r2.speaker: امرؤ القيس
SAMIN-DURR:75:31/r2.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays offers another instance of لا with past-tense negation, though the first two poems suffice for the author.
SAMIN-DURR:75:31/r2.anchor:
واستدل بعضهم أيضا على ذلك بقول امرىء القيس:
4423 كأن دثارا حلقت بلبونه

SAMIN-DURR:75:31/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:31/r3.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:75:31/r3.claim: Makkī says the second لا is independently negative, not conjunctive; the author questions why coordination must be denied.
SAMIN-DURR:75:31/r3.anchor: وقال مكي: " لا " الثانية نفي، وليست بعاطفة، ومعناه: فلم يصدق ولم يصل

SAMIN-DURR:75:31/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:31/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:75:31/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī coordinates the clause with يسأل أيان يوم القيامة, explaining denial of resurrection and of the Messenger and Quran; the commentator finds this far-fetched.
SAMIN-DURR:75:31/r4.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري { فلا صدق ولا صلى } عطفا على الجملة من قوله: { يسأل أيان يوم القيامة }

SAMIN-DURR:75:32/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:32/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:32/r2.claim: It is weak to interpret the first denial as rejecting the Messenger, since that repeats كذب and puts لكن between equivalent statements.
SAMIN-DURR:75:32/r2.anchor: ولهذا يضعف أن يحمل نفي التصديق على نفي تصديق الرسول؛ لئلا يلزم التكرار

ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r1.claim: The person described is Abū Jahl ibn Hishām.
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r1.anchor: يعنى به أبو جهل بن هشام

ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r2.claim: An exegetical saying declares that every community has a Pharaoh and that Abū Jahl ibn Hishām was this community's Pharaoh.
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r2.anchor: وجاء في التفسير إن لكل أمة فرعونا، وإن فرعون هذه الأمة أبو جهل بن هشام

ASAD-NOTES:75:31/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:31/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:31/r1.claim: His repentance is useless: while alive he did not accept truth or pray for enlightenment.
ASAD-NOTES:75:31/r1.anchor: he did not accept the truth

ASAD-NOTES:75:31#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:31#n13/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:31#n13/r1.claim: The interpolation that repentance is useless is needed to complete the sequence and rests on 4:17–18.
ASAD-NOTES:75:31#n13/r1.anchor: based on 4:17-18, which has a definite bearing on the above passage

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p229/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p229/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p229/r3.claim: The Qiyāma figure is worse: unlike the possibly outwardly believing and praying people in Muhammad, he openly denies, turns away, then struts, so he deserves a stronger threat.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p229/r3.anchor: وربما أظهر الأول التصديق والصلاة في حين أن الثاني أظهر التكذيب والتولي، ثم ذهب إلى أهله متبختراً بذاك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r1.claim: Each of the two faults first receives a warning; the second verse restates them as denial and turning away, so the author counts four warnings, one for each fault in both formulations.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r1.anchor: فلا صدق ... أولى لك. ولا صلى ... فأولى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r2.speaker: فتح القدير
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r2.claim: Fatḥ al-Qadīr glosses this as failure to believe in the message and Qur'an and failure to pray to God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r2.anchor: جاء في (فتح القدير) : {فَلاَ صَدَّقَ وَلاَ صلى} أي: لم يصدّق بالرسالة ولا بالقرآن ولا صلى لربه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r3.speaker: قيل
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r3.claim: Another view says he neither believed in his heart nor acted with his body.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r3.anchor: وقيل: فلا آمن بقلبه ولا عمل ببدنه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r4.claim: Denial rejects faith at its foundation—the Messenger and the other pillars of faith—whereas neglect of prayer is a distinct and lesser failure.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r4.anchor: وعدم التصديق أو التكذيب هو إنكار للإيمان من أساسه، فهو لم يصدق بالرسالة ولا ببقية أركان الإيمان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p231/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p231/r1.speaker: أكثر الفقهاء
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p231/r1.claim: Most jurists hold that a Muslim who abandons prayer through laziness, while affirming its obligation, does not thereby leave Islam.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p231/r1.anchor: وقد قال أكثر الفقهاء أن المسلم إذا ترك الصلاة تهاوناً وتكاسلاً غير جاحدٍ لفرضيتها لا يُخْرِجُه ذلك عن الإسلام

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p231/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p231/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p231/r2.claim: The stronger ‘awlā laka’ answers unbelief, while the threat for not praying omits laka; the difference marks the gravity of faith, though the verse ending also supports the omission.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p231/r2.anchor: فقال مقابل {فَلاَ صَدَّقَ} {أولى لَكَ} فذكر {لَكَ} ومقابل {وَلاَ صلى} {فأولى} بحذف (لك) إشارة إلى عظم الإيمان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p231/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p231/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p231/r3.claim: The restatement is harsher: explicit public denial is worse than simply not affirming, and turning away is broader and worse than merely not praying, so the second verse intensifies the first.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p231/r3.anchor: فإنه قال أولاً: {فَلاَ صَدَّقَ} وقال في التأكيد والإعادة: {ولاكن كَذَّبَ} والتكذيب إنما يكون بالإعلان والإشهار

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r1.claim: Rejecting faith is graver than neglecting prayer: a believer who is lax in worship may repent and be forgiven, and does not thereby leave the faith.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r1.anchor: أما إذا كان مؤمناً وتكاسل في الطاعات هذا تُرجى له التوبة والمغفرة ولا يخرج من المِلّة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r2.claim: Adding “لك” to the first warning and omitting it from the second matches the stronger threat to disbelief and signals that the two failings differ in gravity.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r2.anchor: فذكر (لك) ومقابل (ولا صلّى) قال (فأولى) بحذف (لك) إشارة إلى عظم الإيمان وأهميته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r3.claim: Prayer is singled out because it is the most important act of worship.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r4.claim: The later “denied and turned away” restates the lack of belief and prayer; each is reinforced and receives its own warning, yielding four threats.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r4.anchor: وجاء (كذّب) مقابل (لا صدّق) و (تولّى) مقابل (لا صلّى)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p685/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p685/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p685/r1.claim: He reads active denial as more than merely failing to believe, since denial is public avowal; تولّى is broader than simply not praying, which helps explain the sequence.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p685/r1.anchor: فلا صدّق ولكن كذّب وكذّب أكثر من لا صدّق وتقتضي الإعلان والإشهار لذا هي أكثر من ولا صدّق

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p685/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p685/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p685/r2.claim: Fa links each close pair of punishments: death agony with the grave, then resurrection with entry into Hell.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p685/r2.anchor: أما استخدام الفاء في (فأولى) الأولى لأن ما بين العذابين الأوليين عذاب الدنيا وعذاب القبر قريب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p685/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p685/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p685/r3.claim: Thumma marks the long interval from grave to resurrection, thousands of years, and conveys broad distance and separation as well as temporal delay.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p685/r3.anchor: أما استخدام (ثمّ) بين القبر والحشر دلالة على التراخي والفاصل الزمني البعيد بين كل منهما ولأن بين القبر والحشر آلاف السنين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p685/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p685/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p685/r4.claim: The four repetitions of أولى warn the person while alive, dead, on resurrection day, and on entering Hell.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p685/r4.anchor: فالتكرار للفظ (أولى) أربع مرات دلالة على أن الويل لك حياً والويل لك ميتاً والويل لك يوم البعث والويل لك يوم تدخل النار

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p871/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p871/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p871/r1.claim: Past verbs are not normally negated with لا, except when negation is repeated, used as a prayer, or intended for the future; فلا صدّق ولا صلّى exemplifies repetition.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p871/r1.anchor: والفعل الماضي لا يُنفى بـ (لا) إلا في حالات: إما أن يتكرر كما في قوله تعالى (فلا صدّق ولا صلّى)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p871/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p871/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p871/r2.claim: لا زال المطر نازلاً is a prayer for rain to continue; to state that a brother remains absent, he recommends ما زال أخوك غائباً because لا زال would pray for his continued absence.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p871/r2.anchor: ولا نقول "لا زال أخوك غائباً" لأن هذا دعاء عليه أن لا يعود وإنما نقول "ما زال أخوك غائباً"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p871/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p871/r3.speaker: الشاعر
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p871/r3.claim: An unnamed poet uses لا with the past in a prayer, illustrating the optative use of past negation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p871/r3.anchor: حسب المحبين في الدنيا عذابهم تالله لا عذبتهم بعدها سقر

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r4.claim: The unfortunate person neither gives in God's way nor prays to Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r4.anchor: Unfortunate is he who neither spent in the way of God nor prayed to Him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r1.claim: The disbelievers face an exacting journey without provisions: they neither prayed nor spent in God’s way, the two deeds that would benefit them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r1.anchor: no resources and provisions to take along.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r2.claim: A suppressed element after “testified” is supplied from the strong linguistic context and the Sūrah al-Layl parallel, which expresses giving, piety, and belief in the Hereafter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r3.claim: Spending is difficult for those who deny the Hereafter; only confidence that God will return it as an eternal treasure motivates a person to give.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r3.anchor: which motivates a person to spend in the way of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r1.claim: The phrase means the person neither affirmed the Hereafter’s good fate nor spent in God’s way, so it implies both denial of the Hereafter and stinginess.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r1.anchor: rejecting the Hereafter and stinginess are implied in this expression.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r2.claim: Prayer and spending both depend on belief in the Hereafter’s reward; without that belief, these deeds will not arise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r2.anchor: belief in reward in the Hereafter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r3.claim: The verbs contrast: they should have affirmed the Messenger and Hereafter, spent, and prayed, but instead denied the Hereafter and turned away.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r3.anchor: however, they belied the Hereafter and became indifferent.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r4.claim: Prayer and spending in God’s way are the two primary deeds on which the sharīʿah is based, and both depend on firm belief in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r4.anchor: prayer and spending in the way of God

NASHR:v2p112/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p112/r1.speaker: ورش من طريق الأزرق
NASHR:v2p112/r1.claim: Warsh through al-Azraq emphatically pronounces lām after vowelless ẓāʾ in all the cited forms.
NASHR:v2p112/r1.anchor: ومن أظلم، وإذا أظلم، ولا يظلمون، فيظللن فغلظ ورش من طريق الأزرق اللام في ذلك كله

NASHR:v2p112/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p112/r2.speaker: بعض الرواة عن ورش
NASHR:v2p112/r2.claim: Some transmitters report lām softened after ẓāʾ with ṭāʾ, as in the common reading; other sources soften it after ẓāʾ, with al-Hidaya distinguishing open from vowelless ẓāʾ.
NASHR:v2p112/r2.anchor: وروى بعضهم ترقيقها مع الطاء عنه كالجماعة، وهو الذي في العنوان والمجتبى والتذكرة

NASHR:v2p112/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p112/r3.speaker: رواة التغليظ
NASHR:v2p112/r3.claim: Some transmitters emphatically pronounce lām before an imāla-bearing alif because of the preceding letter; several works report this.
NASHR:v2p112/r3.anchor: ففخمها في التبصرة، والكافي، والتذكرة، والتجريد، وغيرها

NASHR:v2p112/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p112/r4.speaker: رواة الترقيق
NASHR:v2p112/r4.claim: Other transmitters soften lām before an imāla-bearing alif because of the imāla; al-Mujtaba and al-Taysir report this.
NASHR:v2p112/r4.anchor: ورققها في المجتبى، وهو مقتضى العنوان، والتيسير، وهو في تلخيص أبي معشر أقيس

NASHR:v2p112/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p112/r5.speaker: رواة الوجهين
NASHR:v2p112/r5.claim: Several sources preserve both emphatic and softened lām before the imāla-bearing alif.
NASHR:v2p112/r5.anchor: والوجهان في الكافي، وتلخيص ابن بليمة، والشاطبية، والإعلان، وغيرها

NASHR:v2p112/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p112/r6.speaker: أصحاب التفريق بين رؤوس الآي وغيرها
NASHR:v2p112/r6.claim: Some soften lām at verse endings for euphony and emphatically pronounce it elsewhere because of the preceding trigger; Ibn al-Jazari cites this as a preferred distinction.
NASHR:v2p112/r6.anchor: فرققوها في رءوس الآي للتناسب وغلظوها في غيرها لوجود الموجب قبلها

NASHR:v2p112/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p112/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p112/r7.claim: The verse-final examples are fa-la saddaqa wa-la salla, wa-dhakara isma rabbihi fa-salla, and idha salla; non-final examples include yasla al-nar.
NASHR:v2p112/r7.anchor: فلا صدق ولا صلى في القيامة وذكر اسم ربه فصلى في سبح إذا صلى في العلق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r2.claim: Most commentators say this passage concerns Abu Jahl; يتمطى describes his characteristic gait, also used by Banu Makhzum, which he often displayed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r2.anchor: فلا صدق ولا صلى، الجمهور: أنها نزلت في أبي جهل وكادت أن تصرح به في قوله: يتمطى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari identifies the man with the person in 75:3, links him to the question in 75:6, and understands him as denying resurrection, the Messenger, and the Quran.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r4.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: يعني الإنسان في قوله: أيحسب الإنسان ألن نجمع عظامه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari's main reading is that he did not believe the Messenger and Quran and did not pray.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r5.anchor: أي لا يؤمن بالبعث؟ فلا صدق بالرسول والقرآن، ولا صلى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers another possibility: فلا صدق means that he did not give alms from his wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد: فلا صدق ماله، يعني فلا زكاه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r7.claim: The author says attaching the clause to يسئل is strained; لا negates past actions here, meaning he neither believed nor prayed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r7.anchor: وكون فلا صدق معطوفا على قوله: يسئل فيه بعد، ولا هنا نفت الماضي، أي لم يصدق ولم يصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r8.claim: The author cites poetry, including a rajaz line, as evidence that لا can negate a past verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r8.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على أن لا تدخل على الماضي فتنصبه، ومثله قوله:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r9.claim: صدق can mean believing God's message, but some derive it from charity; the author prefers charity because it denies alms and prayer while affirming disbelief, as in 74:43–46. The belief reading makes ولكن كذب repetitive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r9.anchor: وقال قوم: هو من الصدقة، وهذا الذي يظهر نفى عنه الزكاة والصلاة وأثبت له التكذيب

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#2/r1.claim: He did not believe what must be believed from God, the Messenger, and the revealed Qur’an.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#2/r1.anchor: فلا صدق أيما يجبتصديقهمن اللهعز وجلوالرسولصص والقرآنالذي أنزل عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#2/r2.claim: He did not perform the prayer made obligatory for him.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#2/r2.anchor: ولا صلى ما فرض عليه أي لم يصدق ولم يصل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#2/r3.claim: The particle لا can enter a past-tense verb, as in the cited poetic usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#2/r3.anchor: فلا داخلة على الماضي كمافي قوله أنتغفر اللهمتغفر جما

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari connects the clause to the preceding question about when resurrection will come: the man mocked and denied it, abandoning both belief and prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#2/r4.anchor: والجملة عطف على قوله سبحانه يسأل أيانيوم القيامة على ما ذهب إليه الزمخشري فالمعنى بناء على ما علمت

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r6.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r6.claim: Qatada says صدق means believing, not giving charity.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r6.anchor: وجعل صدق من التصديق هو المروي عن قتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r7.speaker: قوم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r7.claim: Another group reads صدق as giving charity, in the sense that he neither gave his wealth nor purified it.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r7.anchor: وقالقوم هو من التصديقفلا صدقماله ولا زكاه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r8.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r8.claim: Abu Hayyan favors the charity sense because the passage would then deny both almsgiving and prayer and affirm disbelief, like the description of Hell’s people elsewhere.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r8.anchor: قال أبو حيان وهذاالذييظهر نفي عنهالزكاة والصلاة وأثبت له التكذيب كمافي قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r9.claim: Al-Alusi questions Abu Hayyan’s argument: taking the phrase as disbelief would repeat ولكن كذب and make the contrast follow لا صلى rather than the compatible pair فلا صدق ولا صلى.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r9.anchor: وحمله على نفي التصديقيقتضيأنيكون ولكن كذب تكرارا ولزمأن يكوناستدراكا بعدولا صلى لا بعد فلا صدق لأنهمامتوافقان

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r10.claim: Al-Alusi says coordinating this passage with “he asks when resurrection will come” is remote, though the revelation report about Abu Jahl does not rule it out.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r10.anchor: ثم أنهاستبعد العطفعلى قولهتع إلى يسأل الخ وذكر أن الآية نزلت في أبي جهل وكادت تصرحبه في قوله تعالى يتمطى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r11.claim: The person described is Abu Jahl, who did not believe the Quran or pray to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r11.anchor: يعني: أبا جهل، لم يصدق بالقرآن ولا صلى لله.

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r9.claim: The person is driven to God and His judgment.

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r10.claim: He did not affirm what must be affirmed, or did not give zakāt from his wealth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r10.anchor: ما يجب تصديقه، أو فلا صدق ماله أي فلا زكاة

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r11.claim: He did not perform the obligatory prayer; both clauses refer to the person mentioned in the question about whether humans will be left without purpose.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:25-31/r11.anchor: ما فرض عليه والضمير فيهما للإنسان المذكور

BIQAI-FULL:v8p253#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253#2/r11.claim: The person neither believed the Messenger’s warning about evil deeds nor affirmed the call to spend on good works; the omitted object broadens the denial to all such deeds, and the passage answers the rejection of resurrection in 75:6.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p253#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253#2/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253#2/r12.claim: He did none of the prescribed prayer, obligatory or voluntary, severing both his bond with the Creator and, as law directs, his bond with other people; even disbelievers are addressed by subsidiary duties.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p253#2/r12.anchor: أي ما أمر به من فرض وغيره

DURR-FULL:v8p362/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r6.claim: Qatadah identifies the denier as Abu Jahl: he did not affirm God’s Book or pray, rejected it, turned from obedience, and went home swaggering.
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r6.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {فلا صدق}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r3.claim: Alternatively, the فاء connects to 75:30: the person has left life and is being taken to God without provisions for that meeting; the context implies his knowledge of loss and regret.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الفاء تفريعا وعطفا على قوله : { إلى ربك يومئذ المساق }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r7.claim: Adding ‘nor prayed’ alongside lack of belief makes his condition repugnant and unlike Muslims: he neither believed nor submitted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r7.anchor: وعطف { ولا صلى } على نفس التصديق تشويها له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r8.speaker: الكسائي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r8.claim: Al-Kisa’i says لا can mean لم with past verbs when paired with another negation for two intended actions; Arabs say neither one nor the other, as in Zuhayr’s verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r8.anchor: وهذا معنى قول الكسائي ( ( لا ) بمعنى ( لم ) ولكنه يقرن بغيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r9.claim: An unpaired لا before a past verb is otherwise used for supplication or rarely; 90:11 is effectively repeated negation because ‘the obstacle’ entails freeing, feeding, and believing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p360/r9.anchor: وأما قوله تعالى : { فلا اقتحم العقبة } ( البلد : 11 ) فإنه على تأويل تكرير النفي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.speaker: جمهور المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.claim: Most interpreters say the entire passage concerns Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.anchor: قال جمهور المتأولين: هذه الآية كلها إنما نزلت في أبي جهل بن هشام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r3.claim: The phrasing is elliptical for فلم يصدق ولم يصل; فلا coordinates the verbs, as illustrated by lines of Tarafa and Abu Khirash.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فلا صدق ولا صلى تقديره فلم يصدق ولم يصل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r4.claim: صدق means belief in God's message and religion; some take it as almsgiving, but Ibn Atiyya prefers belief.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r7.claim: Mujahid also reports that the passage was revealed about Abu Jahl.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد: نزلت هذه الآية في أبي جهل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#2/r1.claim: Here lā has the force of lam, giving the sense that he neither believed nor prayed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة لا ها هنا في موضع لم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#2/r2.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#2/r2.claim: The commentators identify the person described as Abu Jahl.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r2.claim: The condemned unbeliever denied truth inwardly and turned away from righteous action outwardly, with no good in either his inner or outward state.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r2.anchor: الكافر الذي كان في الدار الدنيا مكذبا للحق بقلبه، متوليا عن العمل بقالبه،

JISHUMI:v10p7196/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r1.claim: The disbeliever is also addressed by the obligations of prayer and almsgiving.

JISHUMI:v10p7196/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r2.speaker: أبو هاشم
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r2.claim: Abū Hāshim holds that punishment may be deserved for failing to perform an obligation; Abū ʿAlī disagrees.
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r2.anchor: على ما يقوله شيخنا أبو هاشم: أن العقاب قد يستحق على ألا يفعل الواجب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r1.claim: The human is the subject: he rejects resurrection and thus the Messenger and Qur'an, as shown by the surrounding questions about restoring the bones and leaving a person aimless.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r1.anchor: يعني الإنسان في قوله : { أيحسب الإنسان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, فلا صدق ماله means he did not give the alms due from his wealth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r2.anchor: فلا صدق ماله ، بمعنى : فلا زكاة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r3.claim: The passage is said to have been revealed about Abū Jahl.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r17.claim: The passage is about Abu Jahl.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r17.anchor: هذا في أبي جهل , وفيه وجهان

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r18.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r18.claim: He neither believed God’s Book nor prayed to God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r18.anchor: فلا صدق بكتاب الله ولا صلى لله , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r19.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r19.claim: He neither believed the message nor believed the One who sent the messenger.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r19.anchor: فلا صدق بالرسالة ولا آمن بالمرسل , وهو معنى قول الكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r20.claim: A possible synthesis is that he did not believe in his heart or act with his body.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r20.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : فلا آمن بقلبه ولا عمل ببدنه

MUQATIL:75:22-33/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:22-33/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:22-33/r10.claim: Abu Jahl neither believed the Qur'an nor prayed to God.
MUQATIL:75:22-33/r10.anchor: { فلا صدق ولا صلى } [آية: 31] يقول: فلا صدق أبو جهل بالقرآن ولا صلى لله تعالى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#8/r1.claim: He did not affirm the Messenger or the Qur'an.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#8/r1.anchor: بالرسول والقرآن ﴿ ولا صلى ﴾ الإنسان في قوله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#8/r2.claim: The human who did not pray is the one mentioned in “Does man think We will not assemble his bones?”.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#8/r2.anchor: الإنسان في قوله أيحسب الإنسان ان لن يجمع عظامه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#9/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#9/r2.claim: An alternative construes the phrase as withholding charity: he did not give zakat from his wealth.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#9/r2.anchor: أو فلا صدق ما له يعني فلا زكاة

QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r1.claim: Qurtubi’s preferred view, attributed to Ibn Abbas, is that Abu Jahl neither believed nor prayed.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r1.anchor: أي لم يصدق أبو جهل ولم يصل

QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r2.claim: Another view returns the generic human to al-insān at the sūra’s beginning.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r2.anchor: وقيل: يرجع هذا إلى الإنسان في أول السورة، وهو اسم جنس

QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r3.claim: The denial concerns the message; the prayer clause is glossed as supplicating to God and praying for His Messenger.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r3.anchor: أي لم يصدق بالرسالة «ولا صلى» ودعا لربه، وصلى على رسوله

QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r4.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r4.claim: Qatada says he did not believe God’s Book and did not pray to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: فلا صدق بكتاب الله، ولا صلى لله

QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r5.claim: Another view takes denial as failure to give wealth stored with God and prayer as neglect of prescribed prayers.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r5.anchor: وقيل: ولا صدق بمال له، ذخرا له عند الله، ولا صلى الصلوات

QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r6.claim: A further view reads the paired failures as lack of faith in the heart and lack of bodily action.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r6.anchor: وقيل: فلا آمن بقلبه ولا عمل ببدنه

QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r7.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r7.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says lā can mean lam for past negation and is commonly paired with another lā.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r7.anchor: قال الكسائي: «لا» بمعنى لم ولكنه يقرن بغيره تقول العرب

QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r8.claim: Qurtubi distinguishes 90:11: there lā means afalā, why did he not, with the interrogative alif omitted.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r8.anchor: ليس من هذا القبيل لأن معناه أفلا اقتحم أي فهلا اقتحم، فحذف ألف الاستفهام

QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r9.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r9.claim: Al-Akhfash reads lā as past negation, as with 90:11; no paired negative is required, and lā dhahaba means he did not go.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r9.anchor: وقال الأخفش: { فلا صدق } أي لم يصدق كقوله: { فلا اقتحم } أي لم يقتحم

QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r10.speaker: زهير
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r10.claim: Zuhayr’s line is cited as evidence that lā can negate a past verb.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:31/r10.anchor: قول زهير: فلا هو أبداها ولم يتقدم

QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r8.claim: The four faults are failure to believe the Messenger, failure to pray before God, denial, and turning away from prayer; strutting predated denial.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r8.anchor: فترك التصديق خصلة، والتكذيب خصلة، وترك الصلاة خصلة، والتولي عن الله تعالى خصلة
